note.question: How should a firm jointly choose an advertising messenger and product price when messenger type changes the product-match signal structure and consumers must pay a deliberation cost to process the ad?
note.overview: The paper is an information-design game in which a monopolist commits to a messenger-induced signal structure and price while anticipating consumers' Bayesian attention and purchase responses. The messenger is a strategic design choice, not merely an empirical treatment.

components.label: Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the sequential messenger-price, attention, and purchase game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the sequential messenger-price, attention, and purchase game. Section 5 explicitly states that the solution concept is subgame-perfect equilibrium. Consumers use Bayes' rule after a private signal and attend only when its expected benefit covers deliberation cost relative to the no-attention option (Lemma 1). Anticipating those responses, the firm compares full coverage without attention with partial coverage under attention and chooses the messenger-price pair characterized in Proposition 4.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Stage 0: Nature draws each consumer's match value. Stage 1: the firm chooses a highor low-type messenger and a price. Stage 2: after observing messenger and price, each consumer decides whether to incur the deliberation cost and attend to the ad; an attentive consumer receives a private good or bad match signal. Stage 3: the consumer updates beliefs and decides whether to buy.
